newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via system repurchase.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via system repurchase.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system through seven- or five-day system repurchase agreements on Thursday, analysts said.
"There's an ongoing large, seasonal add need," said Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. "We look for a seven-day system, with the possibility of a five-day operation."

James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc, also said he expected the Fed to add temporary reserves to the banking system via seven-day system repurchase agreements. Glassman said he estimated that the Fed needs to add $6.0 billion to $8.0 billion in reserves to the banking system.
"There's a large and growing seasonal add need going into spring," he said.

Though Federal funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate at mid-morning, Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A., also said the Fed was likely to add temporary reserves to the system.
"I could see them doing a system today," he said. "They might be inclined to go term -- a seven-day system, or possibly a five-day operation."
On Wednesday, the Fed added temporary reserves to the banking system through overnight system repurchase agreements and added permanent reserves by buying coupons.
(( -- Ellen Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
